core.title: Estimate feature footprint from plan-artifact, interface and layer cues
core.given: A planner is sizing a feature
core.when: The planner estimates the feature's architectural footprint
core.then: Derive the footprint from the feature's behavior-model plan artifacts, interfaces and component layers by mapping each estimation cue (signal -> footprint element) to its footprint element, rather than guessing a size.
prefer: Behavior-model display/animation signals -> count a screen/view
Behavior-model apply/validate signals -> count an endpoint
Behavior-model reconcile/persist signals -> count a table/migration
Behavior-model notify/retry/queue signals -> count async work
Backend repository-layer components -> count a table/migration
Frontend presentation-layer components -> count the number of screens
avoid: Estimating footprint without tracing it to behavior-model plan artifacts, interfaces and component layers
core.why: Behavior-model verbs, interfaces and component layers are concrete signals of which architectural elements (screens, endpoints, tables, async work, events, integrations) a feature will need, so footprint estimates grounded in them are repeatable and feed footprint scoring.
evidence: Reviewer can trace each footprint element in the estimate back to a behavior-model signal, interface (event / external consumes-produces) or component layer per the cue mapping
Counts of screens, endpoints, tables/migrations, async work, events and integration points are consistent with the cues present in the plan
verification: Checking is content-level traceability over the plan artifacts: every footprint element in the estimate must trace back to a behavior-model signal, interface (event / external consumes-produces) or component layer per the cue mapping, and the stated counts must be consistent with the cues present in the plan; it is not a static source-tree check

The concrete cue map (signal -> footprint element) and its term identifier are supplied by the stack realization's sidecar; the neutral check applies the realization's cue map rather than hard-coding one

fires: Planner writes or revises a feature plan that states an architectural footprint / size estimate
Planner sizes a feature from whatever behavior-model plan artifacts, interfaces and component layers are available, including when some of these inputs are still incomplete or undeclared
doesNotFire: Planner editing docs or acceptances without producing any footprint estimate

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kind names of the stack: which kind is the behavior model whose signals (display/animation, apply/validate, reconcile/persist, notify/retry/queue) drive footprint counting (Bun: the WMBT), and which kinds mark the artifacts being authored for the file_kind activation fact (Bun: feature plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance). The core's 'behavior-model plan artifact' and 'plan artifacts' resolve to these kinds.
profileRequirements.bunValue: feature plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance (behavior model = WMBT)

bunOnly.text: Cue map (term estimation_cue, 'signal -> footprint element'): display_animation -> screen/view; apply_validate -> endpoint; reconcile_persist -> table/migration; notify_retry_queue -> async; new_events -> event count; external_consumes_produces -> integration points; be_repository -> table/migration; fe_presentation -> number of screens
bunOnly.reason: The term id 'estimation_cue' and the raw snake_case cue keys (display_animation, be_repository, fe_presentation, ...) are verifier identifiers of the reference sidecar; the neutral core expresses the same cue mapping in prefer[0..7] and describes the check generically in verification.

classification.note: Already role-level (planner sizing a feature); kept verbatim.
'WMBTs' neutralized to 'behavior-model plan artifacts'; the concrete kind name comes from the profile. Rest of the obligation (cue mapping, rather than guessing a size) kept verbatim.
'WMBT verbs' -> 'behavior-model verbs'; the reasoning (concrete signals, repeatability, feeds footprint scoring) kept verbatim.
Cue source 'WMBT' -> 'behavior-model'; cue (display/animation) and footprint element (screen/view) kept.
Cue source neutralized; 'count an endpoint' kept (endpoint is the generic boundary element).
Cue source neutralized; reconcile/persist -> table/migration kept.
Cue source neutralized; notify/retry/queue -> async work kept.
'Backend repository-layer components' is generic architecture vocabulary (persistence-facing layer), not a stack name; kept.
'Frontend presentation-layer components' maps to the presentation role; kept.
Neutral as-is (counts consistent with cues present in the plan).

The cue mapping is neutral and mirrored in core.prefer; the term id 'estimation_cue' and the raw snake_case key form are realization identifiers kept in bunOnly, while core.verification describes the check generically.
Task terms are rule activation data and already neutral; kept in the core.
Phase 'planning' is neutral; kept with its observability.
Kind values neutralized ('wagon' -> 'product slice', 'WMBT' -> 'behavior model'); the stack's concrete kind names come from the profile.

neutralityNotes: No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. 'WMBT' and 'wagon' have no neutral equivalents inside the sentence, so the core says 'behavior-model plan artifact' and 'product slice' and takes the concrete kind names from roles.plan_artifact.kinds (Bun: feature plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance). 'Repository-layer', 'presentation-layer', 'endpoint', 'table/migration', 'screen/view' and 'async work' are kept as generic architecture vocabulary: they are the footprint elements being counted, not stack names. The verifier's cue-map term id and raw cue keys are realization-only (bunOnly); core.verification names the check generically and defers the concrete cue map to the stack realization.
